pages.ja:
見た事もない景色だった。
頭上には炎の空。
足元には無数の鋼。
戦火の跡なのか、
世界は限りなく無機質で、生きているモノは誰もいない。

pages.en:
—A landscape he had never seen.

Overhead, a sky of flame.

Underfoot, countless swords of steel.

Perhaps this is what remains after a war.

The world is endlessly lifeless, and not one living thing remains.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s a landscape I’ve never seen before.
The fiery sky above.
An infinite number of swords at my feet.
Are they traces of war?
The world is inorganic, and there are no living things.

pages.ja:
灰を含んだ風が、鋼の森を駆け抜ける。
剣は樹木のように乱立し、その数は異様だった。
十や二十ではきかない。
百や二百には届かない。
だが実数がどうであれ、人に数えきれぬのであらば、それは無限と呼ばれるだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
灰を含んだ風が、鋼の森を駆け抜ける。

pages.en:
A wind laden with ash races through the forest of steel.

Swords stand thick as trees, in numbers beyond all reason.

Not ten or twenty.

Not a hundred or two.

Whatever the true number, if no human being could count them, then surely they may be called infinite.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The ashen wind courses through the forest of swords.
The swords stand like trees in a forest.
It’s not just ten or twenty.
Not a hundred or two hundred.
No matter how many there are, if it is impossible for them to be counted, they might as well be infinite.

pages.ja:
大地に突き刺さった幾つもの武具は、使い手が不在のままに錆びていく。
夥しいまでの剣の跡。
pages.jaRuby:
大地に突き刺さった幾つもの武具は、使い手が不在のままに錆びていく。
[ruby text=おびただ]夥しいまでの剣の跡。
pages.en:
Weapons beyond number stand driven into the earth, rusting in the absence of those who once wielded them.

An appalling multitude of scars left by swords.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The tools are rusting without anybody to use them.
A ruin of infinite swords.

まるで墓場のようだと、彼は思った。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
—Looking upon them,

he thought the place resembled a graveyard.
pages.mirrorMoon:
He thinks that…
It is like a graveyard.

pages.en:
…My sight returns.

The sun must have been up for some time. I can feel its steady warmth.

“——That was… a dream.”

I open my eyes blearily and try to recall it.

…A hill of swords.

I dreamed of such a thing because I saw the girl with the sword—Saber—and the cemetery in flames—
pages.mirrorMoon:
…My vision returns.
I don’t know how long it’s been, but I can feel the warm sunlight.
“That dream…”
I open my eyes and recall the dream I was having.
…That hill of swords.
I’m sure I saw that dream because I saw Saber along with the fire in the cemetery…

「あ、お目覚め？ それは結構。大事がなくて何よりだわ」
「は………………？」
と。
同時に、偉そうに見下ろしながら、とんでもなくフツーな一言を述べる遠坂凛。

pages.en:
“Oh, you’re awake? Excellent. I’m glad it was nothing serious.”

“What………………?”

At the same instant, Rin Tohsaka looks imperiously down at me and offers an impossibly ordinary greeting.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, you’re awake? If you’re all right now, that’s good.”
“Huh……?”
Then…
Tohsaka Rin says this in her normal tone while looking down at me.

pages.ja:
「〜〜〜〜〜〜〜っ！」
布団から跳ね起きる。
そのままコンマで壁際まで跳び退いて、ともかく遠坂から距離を取った。

pages.en:
“~~~~~~~~!”

I bolt upright from the futon.

In the same fraction of a second, I spring all the way to the wall and put as much distance between Tohsaka and myself as possible.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“!!!!!!!!!!!!”
I jump up.
I instantly jump back to the wall to get away from Tohsaka.

pages.jaRuby: 「と、とと、とととととと遠坂！？ な、ななな！？ 何故にいま俺の部屋………！！？？」

pages.mirrorMoon: “T-T-T-T-T-Tohsaka!? W-W-What!? Why are you in my room…!!?”

俺は剣の丘
じゃなくて、燃えさかる墓地にいた筈で、近くにいたのはセイバーで、どうして自分の部屋で眠っていてもう朝になっているのか……！？

pages.en:
My thoughts spin in circles.

I was on a hill of swords—no, in a burning cemetery. Saber was near me. So why am I asleep in my own room, and why is it morning already…!?
pages.mirrorMoon:
My head spins.
I should’ve been at that hill of swordsno, at the burning cemetery, so why am I asleep in my room!?

！？」
口にした途端、ますます頭がまわりだした。

一番びっくりしているのは、そう

pages.en:
“T-Tohsaka, why are you here, and what happened to me—!?”

Speaking only makes my head spin faster.

It is not because events have taken some sudden new turn.

The greatest shock of all is that waking to find Tohsaka’s face right in front of mine has made my heart pound this violently.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“T-Tohsaka, why are you here, and what was I doing!?”
My head spins even more after I say that.
It’s not because of this surprising event.
I’m surprised the most at seeing Tohsaka right when I wake upand it’s causing my heart to beat at an abnormal rate.

「驚くんならどっちかに驚きなさいよ。どっちも取れるほど器用じゃないでしょ、衛宮くんは」

“If you’re going to panic, pick one thing to panic about. You aren’t dexterous enough to manage both at once, Emiya.”

Oblivious to my state of mind, Tohsaka remains perfectly cool.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You should just be surprised about one thing. You’re not skilled enough to handle two.”
Tohsaka is just acting cool.

pages.mirrorMoon: “…I see. I guess you carried me here after I fell unconscious.”

pages.jaRuby: 「へえ。なんだ、見た目より頭の回転は速いんだ。混乱しているようでちゃんと物事は考えてるのね。うん、面白い面白い」
pages.en: “Oh? Your mind works faster than you look. Even while you’re confused, you still manage to think things through. Yes, how interesting.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Wow. You’re sharper than I thought. You’re confused, but you’re thinking as well. Yeah, this is certainly interesting.”

pages.ja:
………む。

pages.jaRuby:

………Hmm.

I wish she would stop making remarks that could be either compliments or insults.

…Hm.
I wish she wouldn’t say things that I could take as either insult or praise.

“…Then only half a day has passed.

“If you managed to carry me home, we must have escaped without anyone seeing us.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Then it’s been only half a day?
If you were able to get me home, that means we were able to get away?”

“Exactly. I appreciate your making this easy.”

Apparently satisfied, Tohsaka gives a curt *well, then* and starts away.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yup. I’m glad you’re so smart.”
She must be satisfied.
Saying goodbye, Tohsaka starts to leave.

“What—hey. Where are you going, Tohsaka?”

“Are you still half asleep? Where else would I go? This is your house. It isn’t somewhere I should linger.”

“Huhhey, where are you going?”

Her eyes say,

Her eyes say…
“We’re enemies.”

Last night,

Tohsaka stops and glares at me.

“Wait. Why are you thanking me?”

“Because you helped me. If we’re enemies, I’m all the more grateful for it.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hold on. Why are you thanking me?”
“Well, you helped me, right? I’m even more thankful for that if you’re my enemy.”

“Listen. You still don’t understand, so I’ll make it clear. Thinking that way is going to get you killed.”

“What way?”

“What do you mean if I think like that?”

pages.en:
“————”

Tohsaka delivers the warning in a hard voice, her gaze severe.

…She is undeniably right.

If it is a mistake to sympathize with an enemy as someone like myself, then every needless thought of that kind is also a mistake.

Once I have chosen to fight, the opponent is merely something to defeat.

—Yes. I understand Tohsaka’s position.

But that means—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
Tohsaka speaks with a strong voice and sharp eyes.
…She’s certainly right.
If it’s wrong to feel compassion for an enemy, it is also wrong to consider them to be just like you.
Since I have decided to fight, they are only things I need to defeat.
Yes, I understand her point of view.
But…
